standard_prerequisites.name: Functor precategory B^A
standard_prerequisites.statement: The precategory B^A has functors A -> B as objects and natural transformations as morphisms, with composition and identity defined componentwise.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the precategory in which the isomorphism is taken.

standard_prerequisites.name: Isomorphism in a precategory
standard_prerequisites.statement: An isomorphism is a morphism with a two-sided inverse.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the notion compared componentwise with isomorphisms in B.

core_obligations: Forward direction: if gamma is an isomorphism with inverse delta, then composition in B^A is componentwise, so the identities delta gamma = 1 and gamma delta = 1 imply the componentwise identities at each a, hence each gamma_a is an isomorphism (source lines 341-343).
Converse: suppose each gamma_a is an isomorphism with inverse delta_a, and define a natural transformation delta with those components (source lines 345-346).

Verify the naturality of delta by the displayed chain Ff o delta_a = delta_b o gamma_b o Ff o delta_a = delta_b o Gf o gamma_a o delta_a = delta_b o Gf, using naturality of gamma and the inverse identities (source line 347).
Conclude that gamma delta = 1 and delta gamma = 1 because composition and identities of natural transformations are determined componentwise (source line 348).

proof_roadmap.step: Build the inverse natural transformation and check naturality.
Conclude the two inverse identities componentwise.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.2.4 at source lines 335-339: a natural transformation gamma : F -> G is an isomorphism in the functor precategory B^A if and only if every component gamma_a is an isomorphism in B. The author's proof (source lines 340-349) treats the two directions by different means. The forward direction is immediate because composition in B^A is componentwise (lines 341-343). The converse is a construction: one must define a candidate natural transformation delta with the given componentwise inverses (lines 345-346) and then verify its naturality axiom by an explicit chain in which the naturality of gamma and the two componentwise inverse identities are consumed in a specific order (line 347), before concluding the two inverse identities from the fact that composition and identities of natural transformations are determined on components (line 348). The statement records only the equivalence of the two notions of isomorphism.
